chunks.text:
Atal Pension Yojana is a voluntary pension scheme. The official FAQ describes it as a scheme for
Indian citizens, especially workers in the unorganised sector.

After turning 60, a subscriber receives the chosen guaranteed minimum pension of ₹1,000,
₹2,000, ₹3,000, ₹4,000 or ₹5,000 per month, according to contributions. After the subscriber's
death, the spouse can receive the same pension. After both the subscriber and spouse have died,
the nominee can receive the accumulated pension wealth described in the FAQ.

A new subscriber must be an Indian citizen aged 18 to 40 and have a savings bank account or
post-office savings bank account. Since 1 October 2022, a person who is or has been an
income-tax payer on the application date cannot open a new APY account. This restriction does
not close APY accounts opened by 30 September 2022.

The contribution depends on the subscriber's age at joining and the pension amount chosen.
Contributions are collected by automatic debit from the savings bank or post-office savings bank
account. The subscriber can choose monthly, quarterly or half-yearly contributions.

Approach the bank branch or post office where the savings account is held. A person without such
an account must first open one. Only one APY account is permitted per person.

This note covers the PM-JAY senior-citizen benefit described in the National Health Authority's
FAQ. It does not describe other PM-JAY eligibility groups.

All senior citizens aged 70 or above are eligible for this benefit regardless of economic
status. Age is determined from the date of birth recorded in Aadhaar.

Eligible senior citizens can receive free medical treatment up to ₹5 lakh under the scheme. The
National Health Authority FAQ says treatment can be accessed from the first day of enrolment,
without a waiting period.

Aadhaar-based eKYC is required for enrolment and issuance of an Ayushman card. The FAQ says
Aadhaar is the only document needed for this enrolment. Apply through beneficiary.nha.gov.in or
the Ayushman App. Eligible family members aged 70 or above can be added after the first member
is enrolled.

chunks.schemeName: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS)
chunks.text:
The official scheme website says MGNREGS provides a legal guarantee of at least 100 days of
wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to
do unskilled manual work.

chunks.schemeName: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS)
chunks.text:
This note covers only the employment guarantee stated on the official scheme website. It does
not describe registration steps, wage rates, unemployment allowance or local implementation
rules.

PM-KISAN is a Central Sector scheme funded by the Government of India. State and Union Territory
administrations identify the farmer families eligible under the scheme guidelines. For this
scheme, a family means husband, wife and minor children.

Eligible landholding farmer families receive ₹6,000 per year in three equal instalments. The
money is transferred directly to beneficiaries' bank accounts. eKYC is mandatory for registered
farmers.

State and Union Territory administrations identify eligible farmer families under the scheme
guidelines and land records. Institutional landholders are excluded.

The portal lists these exclusion categories: current or former holders of constitutional posts;
current or former ministers, legislators, municipal corporation mayors and district panchayat
chairs; serving or retired government, public sector and regular local body employees, except
Multi Tasking Staff and Class IV / Group D employees; retired pensioners receiving at least
₹10,000 per month, with the same employee exception; people who paid income tax in the last
assessment year; and registered professionals such as doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered
accountants and architects who practise their profession.

The PM-KISAN portal provides New Farmer Registration and a Know Your Status service. The portal
also says State and Union Territory administrations identify eligible families. eKYC is
mandatory for registered farmers to receive scheme instalments.

The portal says benefits may be temporarily withheld for suspected cases such as land ownership
acquired after 1 February 2019 or more than one family member receiving benefits, until physical
verification is completed. It directs farmers to check Know Your Status on the PM-KISAN website
or mobile app for details.

PMSBY is a one-year personal accident insurance cover that can be renewed each year. It covers
death or disability caused by an accident.

The official FAQ lists ₹2 lakh for accidental death and ₹2 lakh for total and irrecoverable
loss of both eyes, both hands or feet, or one eye together with one hand or foot. It lists
₹1 lakh for total and irrecoverable loss of sight in one eye or use of one hand or foot.

The FAQ lists a premium of ₹20 per member per year. It is deducted from the member's bank or
post-office account in one instalment by automatic debit, with the subscriber's consent.

Individual account holders of participating banks or post offices aged 18 to 70 can join. A
person with multiple accounts can join through only one bank or post-office account.

Ask a participating bank or post office to enrol. The FAQ says the premium is collected by
automatic debit after the subscriber gives consent.

An eligible beneficiary is an adult woman from a poor household who submits the scheme's
deprivation declaration. The household must not already have an LPG connection registered to
any family member listed in its family-composition document. A PMUY connection is issued in the
name of an adult woman.

The official FAQ describes a security-deposit-free LPG connection with no installation charge,
a free first refill, and a free two-burner stove. The FAQ says the beneficiary does not pay the
distributor for these listed items.

Apply online using the form on pmuy.gov.in, submit an application at an LPG distributorship, or
ask a nearby Common Service Centre for help. The FAQ says online self-submission has no fee; a
₹20 charge applies when a Common Service Centre submits the application.

The FAQ lists the applicant's application and KYC form, recent photograph, and Aadhaar; Aadhaar
details for adult family members shown on the family-composition document; address proof; bank
account details; a ration card or other government family-composition document; and the signed
deprivation declaration. Migrant applicants may use the prescribed self-declaration for address
and family composition.
Biometric Aadhaar authentication is mandatory and is carried out by the LPG distributor.
